faqs.a:
(a)
Disposition of dangerous or worthless property.
The provisions of
section 62-95
do not apply to the disposition of dangerous or worthless property. The custodian
               may destroy, or order destroyed, each and every article of the following described
               property which is not subject to the jurisdiction of any court or quasi-judicial authority:
               burglary tools; explosives; armor or bulletproof clothing; gambling apparatus; beer,
               wine, spirituous liquors or fermented malt beverages; cigarettes or tobacco products;
               soiled, bloody, or unsanitary clothing; solids or liquids of unknown or uncertain
               composition; drugs, medicines, pharmaceutical products, hallucinogenic substances,
               or hypodermic syringes or needles; obscene pictures, images, or objects contained
               in or on any media or format; any poisonous or noxious solids or liquids; or any other
               property which reasonably might result in injury to the health or safety of the public
               or be the subject of unlawful use.
(1)
Notwithstanding the above, the custodian may, at his sole discretion, deliver to the
               director for auction in accordance with the purchasing and contracts ordinance any
               unopened fine wine, spirituous liquor, fermented malt beverage, or other alcoholic
               beverage which, in the opinion of the custodian, may be of value to connoisseurs.
(b)
Disposition of automobiles, stray animals, or certain other property.
The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to the sale of abandoned automobiles
               as addressed in the state statutes regarding the removal and disposal of abandoned
               vehicles; the disposition of lost or stray animals; or to the disposition of any property
               which is governed by the terms of any specific ordinance or applicable statute.
(c)
Disposition of firearms, cartridges, ammunition, or other weapons except explosives.
The provisions of
section 62-95
do not apply to the disposition of firearms, cartridges, ammunition, or other weapons.
               These items shall be disposed of as follows:
(1)
Dangerous, illegal, or contraband weapon.
Any weapon that is dangerous, illegal, or deemed to be contraband pursuant to state
               or federal law shall also be deemed forfeited and shall become the sole property of
               the city.
(2)
Lawful possession apparent.
If the custodian has determined that the item may be lawfully possessed by the owner
               or other person entitled to possession of the item, or if there exists a valid court
               order directing that the item be released to such person, the custodian shall release
               the item in accordance with the custodian's determination or the court order.
(3)
Lawful possession not apparent.
If the custodian has determined that the owner or other person thought to be entitled
               to possession of the item is no longer legally entitled to possession of the item
               pursuant to federal, state, or local law, and if there exists no valid court order
               directing that the item be released to any person, the item shall be disposed of as
               follows:
(i)
The custodian shall notify the owner or other person thought to be legally entitled
               to possession of the item that he is no longer legally entitled to possess the item
               because of a legal disqualification. The notice shall contain a description of the
               item or items, along with a forfeiture notice as set forth in subsection
62-97
(c)(5).
(a)
The owner or other person may, within 30 days of the date of the notification, appeal
               the disqualification decision as set forth in subsection
62-95
(a)(9), or file with the custodian a written designation of another person who does
               not reside with the owner or other person, as the third-party recipient of the item.
               If the written designation is not timely filed, any claim of ownership to such item
               shall be deemed to be waived, the item shall be deemed forfeited, and it shall become
               the sole property of the city.
(i)
The owner, other person, or third-party recipient shall, within 14 days of the designation,
               provide to the custodian all information necessary to determine if the recipient is
               qualified to possess the item. Should the necessary information not be provided, the
               claim to ownership of the item shall be deemed waived, the item shall be deemed forfeited,
               and it shall become the sole property of the city.
(ii)
Should the custodian determine the recipient is not legally entitled to possession
               of the item the custodian shall notify the owner, other person and the third-party
               recipient of such fact. The owner or other person may, within 30 days of the date
               of the notification, file with the custodian a written designation of an alternate
               third-party recipient, which shall be processed as set forth in this subsection. If
               the written designation is not timely filed, any claim of ownership shall be deemed
               to be waived, the item shall be deemed forfeited, and it shall become the sole property
               of the city. Should the alternate recipient be deemed by the custodian as not legally
               entitled to the item, the item shall be deemed forfeited, and it shall become the
               sole property of the city.
(iii)
In the event any third-party recipient is deemed qualified to possess the item, the
               custodian shall release the item upon payment of all fees and costs incurred by the
               custodian in processing and investigating the release to the recipient.
(4)
Municipal court case.
In any matter where a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or other weapon is seized during
               the investigation of a municipal ordinance violation, or seized in a situation where
               no charges are filed, the custodian may release the item in accordance with the law,
               except that if for any reason, the custodian is unable to determine whether the item
               may be lawfully released, or is otherwise unable to release the item for any reason,
               the municipal court shall, upon motion of the owner or the city attorney for disposition
               of said item, convene a hearing on the disposition of the item. After taking evidence
               on the disposition of the property, the court shall order the return or other disposition
               of each and every item in the custody of the custodian. The court may hold such an
               order in abeyance until after any relevant case in the court has been closed.
(5)
Notice and appeal.
In any case where a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or other weapon is subject to
               impending forfeiture pursuant to subsections
62-97
(c)(1) or (3), the custodian shall in any notification to an owner, other person,
               or third-party recipient, state that the item may be forfeited. The custodian may
               include a copy of
section 62-97
(c) in any written notice concerning a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or other weapon
               to satisfy this requirement. In any case where a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or
               other weapon is deemed forfeited, the custodian shall retain the forfeited item for
               30 days after the date of the notification to allow for an appeal in accordance with
               subsection
62-95
(a)(9).
(6)
Competing claims.
In any case where there is a competing claim for a firearm, cartridge, ammunition,
               or other weapon, the claims shall be resolved in accordance with subsection
62-95
(a)(6).
(7)
Record to be kept.
In any case where a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or other weapon is deemed forfeited,
               the custodian may:
(i)
Order the item destroyed;
(ii)
Order that the item be retained by the police department for use in training or for
               other official purposes; or
(iii)
Following consultation with the director, order that the item be otherwise disposed
               of.
Whenever an item is retained by the police department for use in training or for other
               official purposes, the item shall be accounted for on the property records of the
               police department until such item is depleted or otherwise disposed of.
(8)
Any release of a firearm, cartridge, ammunition, or other weapon must be done in accordance
               with applicable police department policy.
(
Ord. No. 4238, § 1, 12-6-2010
)
